# Istravex

> Open-source XDR conformance and replay kit for Stellar. Checks that SDKs decode and re-encode XDR faithfully, and that indexers store the right records for the right accounts, using a shared, versioned corpus of rare but valid Stellar XDR. Proposed for Stellar Community Fund (SCF) #46, RFP 2. Status: proposed for funding; a working kit (corpus, provenance verifier, SDK runners, mock RPC, replay, Go linter, upstream pilot) is in the repository.

## Docs

- [Repository](https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex): site, corpus, capture scripts, runners, replay harness
- [Corpus format](https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex/tree/main/corpus): manifest schema and fixtures
- [Full proposal (Markdown)](/proposal.md): scope, problem, deliverables, draft manifest, milestones, maintenance
- [SCF RFP Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/rfp-track): official RFP scope

## Corpus and results (real data)

- 20 fixtures across 6 CAPs and 14 patterns: 6 mainnet (4 found by scanning 400,000 mainnet ledgers), 2 testnet, 10 generated on a pinned stellar-core at mainnet's protocol 29, 2 synthetic (labelled; bytes a decoder must refuse):
  - cap27-muxed-payment-pubnet-0001: mainnet ledger 65474279; USDC payment to muxed ID 1764988090084626463 (above 2^53; JavaScript Number() reads 1764988090084626400)
  - cap15-fee-bump-pubnet-0001: mainnet ledger 65474309; fee source differs from inner source; fee charged 40354 stroops vs 46340 debited in fee changes before the Soroban refund
  - cap40-signed-payload-signer-{testnet,local}-0001: ed25519 signed-payload signer (account LedgerEntryData); reproduces wallet-backend#729
  - cap73-sac-trust-{testnet,local}-0001: trustline created by SAC trust(), with no changeTrust op; reproduces wallet-backend#731
  - cap27-muxed-max-id-local-0001: muxed source ID 2^53+1 to muxed destination ID 2^64-1; reproduces js-stellar-sdk#1785
  - cap46-muxed-soroban-source-local-0001: ExtendFootprintTtl from an M-address source; reproduces wallet-backend#716
  - cap38-pool-issuer-order-local-0001: pool-share trustline whose issuers sort differently as strkeys and as bytes; reproduces js-stellar-sdk#1766
  - cap46-scmap-host-order-local-0001: 10-entry map with mixed-type and colliding keys; reproduces js-stellar-sdk#1766 and #1789
  - cap46-nested-auth-local-0001: six-level Soroban authorization tree
  - base-memo-non-utf8-local-0001: 28-byte memo text that isn't UTF-8
  - base-max-length-vectors-local-0001: 100 operations, 20 signatures, 20 signers
  - base-over-max-length-synthetic-0001, cap46-scval-limits-synthetic-0001: 101 operations, 29-byte memo, 2^32-1 length prefixes, 2,000-deep ScVal
  - cap27-muxed-payment-pubnet-0002 (muxed ID above 2^63), cap73-sac-trust-pubnet-0001 (mainnet USDC trust() via SAC), cap46-nested-auth-pubnet-0001 (auth tree depth 4), base-max-length-vectors-pubnet-0001: from mainnet
  - base-max-amount-local-0001: a payment of i64::MAX stroops; reproduces stellar-etl#454
  - generation on standalone stellar-core 30.0.0 is byte-reproducible (seeded keys, fixed close times), for any network passphrase
- Provenance: 205/205 checks; every non-synthetic fixture is byte-identical to the canonical LedgerCloseMeta of its ledger
- SDK conformance: 278/280 checks across @stellar/stellar-sdk 17.4.0, go-stellar-sdk 0.9.0, stellar-xdr 30.0.0, Python stellar-sdk 17.0.1 and java-stellar-sdk 6.0.0; the two failures are known upstream bugs (StellarCN/py-stellar-base#1250, lightsail-network/java-stellar-sdk#832); js-stellar-sdk 17.2.0 and 17.2.1 fail exactly the checks for #1766, #1785 and #1789
- Replay: the naive indexer is wrong on 9/9 cases; the reference indexer is right on 9/9; ledgers served over mock RPC getLedgers or the Galexie data-lake layout (filesystem or S3)
- Upstream pilots: stellar-etl v2.8.34 gets 7/11 right and reproduces its open issues #454 (float amounts) and #460 (no SAC trust() effect); stellar/wallet-backend @ 3e22515 indexes 11/11 fixtures correctly over RPC and over the data lake; wallet-backend#729, #731 and #716 reproduce on the commits before their fixes and pass on the fixes; istravex-lint finds 1 latent IX001 (unused memo helper) on main, and IX003/IX002 on the pre-fix commits
- Findings: 19 in corpus/findings.json (https://api.istravex.com/v1/findings), each with severity, upstream issue, corpus entry and the checks it explains
- CAP audit: 70 live CAPs, 40 change XDR, 5 covered
- Hardening guide: https://docs.istravex.com/guide/overview (reviewed and confirmed by a Stellar Core engineer); field-by-field table at https://docs.istravex.com/guide/validated-fields
- stellar-core goldens: all three SDKs round-trip 15,306/15,306 LedgerCloseMeta frames from core's --check-lcm data (v30.0.0)
- Docs: https://docs.istravex.com
- Security policy: https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex/blob/main/SECURITY.md (private vulnerability reporting; exploitable findings disclosed privately first via SDF's bug bounty)
- Guides: https://docs.istravex.com/guides/sdk-conformance (SDK), https://docs.istravex.com/guides/indexer-ci (indexer CI), https://docs.istravex.com/guides/fixtures-in-tests (app tests), https://docs.istravex.com/guides/hosted-api (API)
- API: https://api.istravex.com (OpenAPI: https://api.istravex.com/openapi.json)
- Mock Stellar RPC: https://rpc.istravex.com/{pubnet,testnet,local}

## Deliverables

1. Versioned XDR corpus + CAP coverage audit (captured ledgers and pinned stellar-core recipes; synthetic entries labelled; checked against `--check-lcm` goldens where available)
2. Offline indexer replay harness (mock Stellar RPC `getLedgers`, reference adapter for `wallet-backend`; verdicts: correct, incorrect, dropped)
3. Cross-SDK conformance runner (pinned JavaScript, Go, Rust adapters; decode, byte-for-byte re-encode, native conversion checks; wide integers kept at full precision)
4. Go linter (3 rules: trusting Core pass-through fields; unbounded recursive XDR; participants derived from the envelope instead of ledger meta) + indexer-hardening guide
5. Upstream pilot against `wallet-backend` with a triaged findings report

## Manifest fields

id, cap_ids, protocol_version, network, xdr_type, xdr_path, sha256, source, synthetic, expected_decoded, expected_indexed. Wide integers are decimal strings.

## Milestones

1. Corpus and reference replay
2. Conformance and linting
3. Upstream pilot and public release

## Commitments (proposed)

Apache 2.0; named maintainer for 6 months after launch, through the first protocol upgrade after delivery; no usage telemetry.
